vuln_id: ARVO arvo:51735 / krb5 PAC parser header-length overflow out-of-bounds read

project.name: MIT Kerberos 5
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the prepared checkout at `70f61d417261ca17efe3d60d180033bea2da60b0`, which is an ancestor of both metadata commits `fa62bd33a0c0889c083999c0289ffa81a5d51e7b` and `ea92d2f0fcceb54a70910fa32e9a0d7a5afc3583`. That staged tree still contains the same vulnerable `krb5_pac_parse()` arithmetic, and the saved `patch.diff` applies the same `MAX_BUFFERS` pre-check plus later PAC buffer bounds hardening. The staged workspace also contains an untracked harness `fuzzing/Fuzz_pac.c` that forwards raw fuzz bytes into `krb5_pac_parse()`.

staged_source_snapshot.description: This is the exact staged vulnerable source tree whose line map matches the saved ASan crash. It also contains the untracked `fuzzing/Fuzz_pac.c` harness used by Stage 01.

classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports `use-after-poison` because AFL++ allocates a larger 1 MiB input buffer and user-poisons bytes beyond the current testcase length. At source level the witnessed defect is a 4-byte read past the logical end of a 15-byte PAC blob, enabled by 32-bit overflow in `header_len = PACTYPE_LENGTH + (cbuffers * PAC_INFO_BUFFER_LENGTH)` when `cbuffers == 0x10000000`.

bug_description.original: Integer overflows exist in PAC parsing within the krb5_parse_pac() function. Buffer counts large enough can threaten integer overflow in the header length and memory length calculations, and there is a risk of integer overflows when checking the length of each buffer. In MIT krb5 releases 1.8 and later, an authenticated attacker may be able to cause a KDC or kadmind process to crash by reading beyond the bounds of allocated memory, resulting in a denial of service. A privileged attacker may similarly be able to cause a Kerberos or GSS application service to crash. On 32-bit platforms, an attacker can also cause insufficient memory to be allocated for the result, potentially leading to remote code execution in a KDC, kadmind, or GSS or Kerberos application server process. An attacker with the privileges of a cross-realm KDC may be able to extract secrets from a KDC process's memory by having them copied into the PAC of a new ticket.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the crash against the staged krb5 checkout `70f61d417261ca17efe3d60d180033bea2da60b0`, an ancestor of the metadata vulnerable and fixed commits, so this trace is grounded to that exact line map plus the staged untracked harness `fuzzing/Fuzz_pac.c`. The exact staged `poc` is 15 bytes: `00 00 00 10 00 00 00 00 06 ff ff ff 00 00 f5`. The harness accepts `Size == 15` and passes the bytes unchanged to `krb5_pac_parse(context, Data, Size, &pac)`. Inside `krb5_pac_parse()`, bytes 0..3 decode little-endian as `cbuffers = 0x10000000` and bytes 4..7 decode as `version = 0`, so the parser stays on the PAC path. The vulnerable `header_len = PACTYPE_LENGTH + (cbuffers * PAC_INFO_BUFFER_LENGTH)` expression then performs 32-bit arithmetic because `cbuffers` is `krb5_ui_4`: `0x10000000 * 16` wraps to `0`, so `header_len` becomes only `8`. The subsequent guard `if (len < header_len) return ERANGE;` therefore treats the 15-byte witness as having a complete PAC header even though one `PAC_INFO_BUFFER` descriptor needs 16 bytes after the fixed 8-byte PACTYPE header. On the witnessed run the parser reaches the first loop iteration, successfully reads `buffer->ulType` from bytes 8..11, advances `p` to offset 12, and then executes `buffer->cbBufferSize = load_32_le(p)`. That second 4-byte little-endian read has only three logical input bytes left (`00 00 f5`), so it touches the first AFL++-poisoned byte at offset 15. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `use-after-poison READ of size 4` with top frame `load_32_le` and caller `krb5_pac_parse:343`. The staged patch resolves this exact witness by rejecting `cbuffers < 1 || cbuffers > MAX_BUFFERS` before the overflow-prone header-length arithmetic; its later `Offset`/`cbBufferSize` hardening covers separate malformed PAC layouts that this 15-byte witness never reaches.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that materializes attacker-controlled PAC state. It parses the fuzz bytes into the buffer-count field that later overflows the header-length calculation and controls the PAC buffer loop bound.
source.value_from: The exact staged 15-byte `poc` is `00 00 00 10 00 00 00 00 06 ff ff ff 00 00 f5`. Bytes 0..3 decode little-endian as `cbuffers = 0x10000000` (268435456).

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink callsite. The parser requests a 4-byte read for `cbBufferSize` from `p == ptr + 12` even though only three logical input bytes remain.
sink.note: The saved ASan top frame is the inlined helper `load_32_le` at `src/include/k5-platform.h:703`, and frame 1 is this exact callsite at `pac.c:343`. The shadow bytes `00 07 f7` in `sanitizer_trace.txt` show bytes 8..14 are addressable and byte 15 is user-poisoned, so this 4-byte read crosses the logical 15-byte testcase boundary by one byte.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The parser multiplies the attacker-controlled 32-bit `cbuffers` count by 16 before any upper-bound check. For the witness value `0x10000000`, that 32-bit multiply wraps to zero, so `header_len` becomes `8` and the later length check validates only the fixed PACTYPE header instead of the required `PAC_INFO_BUFFER` descriptors.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds `if (cbuffers < 1 || cbuffers > MAX_BUFFERS) return ERANGE;` immediately before this line, confirming that the missing obligation on the witnessed path is to bound `cbuffers` before the overflow-prone arithmetic. The patch's later `buffer->Offset` hardening is not needed to explain this saved crash.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first four attacker-controlled bytes become the oversized 32-bit buffer count that overflows `header_len` and later drives the PAC buffer loop.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Bytes 0..3 of the exact witness are `00 00 00 10`, so this statement materializes `cbuffers = 0x10000000`.

parser_admitted.description: This is the size gate that admits the malformed PAC to buffer parsing on the witnessed path. Because step 3 wrapped `header_len` to `8` while `len == 15`, the function does not reject the truncated first `PAC_INFO_BUFFER` and continues into the loop.

evidence_limitations: The staged reproducing source is checkout `70f61d417261ca17efe3d60d180033bea2da60b0` plus the untracked harness `fuzzing/Fuzz_pac.c`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `fa62bd33a0c0889c083999c0289ffa81a5d51e7b`. The staged checkout is an ancestor of both metadata commits and contains the same vulnerable `krb5_pac_parse()` arithmetic and the same fixing patch hunk.

The saved run is a 64-bit AFL++/ASan execution and proves the logical-input over-read path only. It does not dynamically validate the separate 32-bit insufficient-allocation or memory-disclosure consequences mentioned in `sample_info.json`.

The staged patch also hardens `buffer->Offset` and `buffer->cbBufferSize` validation for later PAC records. This 15-byte witness crashes before any `Offset` field is read, so the grounded root cause for this sample is only the missing `cbuffers` bound before `header_len` calculation.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged untracked harness accepts the exact 15-byte witness and forwards it unchanged to `krb5_pac_parse`, which parses `cbuffers = 0x10000000` and `version = 0` from the first eight bytes.

The vulnerable `header_len = 8 + cbuffers * 16` arithmetic wraps to `8`, so the subsequent `len < header_len` gate fails to reject a 15-byte blob that does not contain one full 16-byte `PAC_INFO_BUFFER` descriptor.

After `pac->pac->cBuffers = cbuffers` stores the huge attacker count into the PAC object, the loop reads that field as its bound, enters the first iteration, successfully reads `ulType` from bytes 8..11, and advances the cursor to offset 12.

The next `cbBufferSize` read starts at offset 12 although only three logical input bytes remain, so `load_32_le` touches the poisoned byte at offset 15 and reproduces the saved AddressSanitizer `use-after-poison READ of size 4`.

fine_trace.note: Harness boundary only. The exact staged witness is 15 bytes, so it passes the harness length filter `10 <= Size <= 5120` and is forwarded unchanged as `ptr = Data` and `len = Size` into `krb5_pac_parse()`.
Source. Bytes 0..3 of the witness (`00 00 00 10`) are parsed as `cbuffers = 0x10000000`, and `p` advances to the version field at byte 4.
Bytes 4..7 decode as `version = 0`, so the version rejection is not taken. `p` now points at byte 8, the start of the first claimed `PAC_INFO_BUFFER` record.

Root cause. `cbuffers` is a 32-bit `krb5_ui_4`, so `0x10000000 * 16` wraps to `0` before assignment to `size_t`. The computed `header_len` therefore becomes only `8`, not the true `4294967304` bytes implied by the claimed number of PAC buffer descriptors.

With `len == 15` from step 0 and wrapped `header_len == 8` from step 3, this guard is false. The parser therefore treats the witness as having a complete PAC header even though a single `PAC_INFO_BUFFER` descriptor alone requires 16 bytes after the fixed 8-byte PACTYPE header.

After the earlier `krb5_pac_init()` and `realloc()` path succeeds on the witnessed run, the parsed attacker count `0x10000000` is written into the heap PAC object's `cBuffers` field. This recorded field state is what the upcoming loop predicate reads as its bound.

The loop bound now reads the installed heap field from step 5, so iteration `i = 0` starts even though only seven bytes remain after the fixed 8-byte header, far less than one full 16-byte `PAC_INFO_BUFFER` descriptor.

The first field read of the first claimed buffer record succeeds because bytes 8..11 are present in the witness. After this read, `p` advances to byte 12 and only bytes 12..14 remain logically addressable.

Sink. This starts a 4-byte little-endian read at byte 12, but the 15-byte witness has only three remaining bytes there (`00 00 f5`). `load_32_le` therefore touches the user-poisoned byte at offset 15, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `use-after-poison READ of size 4` with top frame `load_32_le` and caller `krb5_pac_parse:343`.

allocation_context.note: ASan says the faulting address is 15 bytes inside a 1048576-byte driver allocation created here. AFL++ user-poisons bytes beyond the current testcase size, so the source-level one-byte-over-end read from the 15-byte logical input surfaces as `use-after-poison` instead of a plain heap-buffer-overflow.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds `if (cbuffers < 1 || cbuffers > MAX_BUFFERS) return ERANGE;` before `header_len = PACTYPE_LENGTH + (cbuffers * PAC_INFO_BUFFER_LENGTH);`, which is the exact missing precondition on the saved witness. Stage 02 did not perform fixed-version dynamic validation.

format.name: 15-byte truncated PAC header with overflowed buffer count
format.contract: Use exactly the staged 15-byte file `00 00 00 10 00 00 00 00 06 ff ff ff 00 00 f5` (SHA-256 `fa3922d2b224987ad5aa2df55a50b65f818dabf3c93136bae4e17ebf36abf157`). Bytes 0..3 must decode little-endian as `cbuffers = 0x10000000`, bytes 4..7 must decode as `version = 0`, and the input must end after the seven-byte prefix of the first `PAC_INFO_BUFFER` record so that only bytes 8..14 exist. That exact layout makes `cbuffers * 16` wrap to zero, leaves `header_len == 8`, allows the parser to read `ulType` from bytes 8..11, and then causes `buffer->cbBufferSize = load_32_le(p)` to start a 4-byte read at offset 12 with only three logical bytes remaining. Stage 02 does not generalize beyond this exact witness and observed `krb5_pac_parse()` path.
